https://cabar.asia/en/iwpr-and-inidi-pf-.body: © CABAR - Central Asian Bureau for Analytical Reporting Please make active links to the source, when using materials from this website На русском Қазақша IWPR and the INIDI Public Foundation have completed the “Civil Society for Kazakhstan” project with the final conference event, funded by the European Union, and have taken stock of three years of work. On 24-25 September 2026, the CS4K project’s final conference, “Time to Preserve Meaning,” took place in Almaty. Participants discussed the project’s results and talked about how civil society in Kazakhstan can develop amid today’s challenges. The conference was more than a closing event. It was a space for open dialogue about restoring meaning to civic work, mutual support, solidarity, and finding joint solutions. Representatives of government bodies, civil society organizations, international partners, donors, experts, the media, and activists took part. The central message of the meeting was that even as civic space narrows, real change is possible through professionalism, partnership, solidarity, and dialogue. Day 1: Stories of change and discussions The first day, 24 September, opened with a discussion of the context in which civil society operates today. Participants then heard “stories of change”: ten local advocacy initiatives supported under the project were presented in two blocks of five. A general discussion of all ten initiatives followed. Key results of the initiatives presented: Diabetic Parents’ Committee: insulin pumps for adults. The team drew on data from 465 patients, the opinions of 20 doctors, and a review of 21 international studies. Order No. 57 was signed on 25 May 2026 and will take effect on 1 January 2027. Wings of Liberty PF: personal data protection for NGOs. The first systematic study covered 111 organizations in 17 regions. It found that only 39.6% of organizations have an internal data protection policy, and only 27.9% have appointed a responsible person. Recommendations were prepared in two languages, and a dialogue with the relevant ministry has begun. Just Support PF: protecting children from bullying and violence. The organization’s proposals are reflected in the national plan “Children of Kazakhstan” for 2026-2030, and in June 2026 Just Support joined the ministry’s permanent NGO expert group. Support for the Initiatives PF: rural women’s access to healthcare. The study covered 582 respondents and 27 interviews. Of 24 recommendations, 10 have been implemented or are in progress: a rural outpatient clinic was renovated, specialists’ schedules were expanded, and video monitoring was introduced to prevent fictitious appointment records. Civil Alliance of Pavlodar Region: pasture management. Following a study of 531 households and 11 recommendations, a plan was published and a coordination and oversight body was designated. Meyirim Public Association: workplace harassment. 155 respondents took part in the survey, 64% of whom reported perceiving harassment in the workplace, and 44 stories were collected. The Ministry of Labor reported that the term “sexual harassment” has been included in the draft amendments to the Labor Code. My Home Public Association: reintegration of women after release. Based on a study involving one hundred women, a model for a non-governmental “one-stop-shop” service was developed. 22 women received comprehensive assistance, and 18 of them were provided with temporary housing. Korgan-M Republican Public Association: inclusive emergency preparedness. A survey of more than 430 people showed that over 70% had difficulties during evacuation and 34% would be unable to evacuate on their own. The national Ministry of Emergency Situations circulated the report to its units, and local measures and a request for training followed. Daris-2016 Public Association: education of migrant children. Based on more than twenty resolved cases, 25 recommendations were prepared. Government Resolution No. 56 of 29 January 2026 added a separate section on migrant children to the “Children of Kazakhstan” Concept. Mama Pro PF : psychological support for parents of children with disabilities. 1,119 people took part in the survey: 73% live with constant anxiety, and only 5.7% had used state-provided psychological help. Responses were received from three ministries, and a pilot for ten mothers will launch in autumn 2026. The strongest cases share a common approach: the problem is framed through the concrete experience of a person or community, backed by data, and translated into a specific regulatory, budgetary, or administrative mechanism. Beneficiaries, specialists, and the bodies responsible for implementation were involved, and the result was secured through a document, a designated responsibility, or a working service. Materials and details on each of the ten supported projects are available via the link. In the second half of the day, participants worked in a World Café format. Tables discussed: human rights in everyday life and how to bring change closer to people; the narrowing civic space and ways to preserve freedom of action and NGO resilience; local advocacy and what actually works in the regions; the safety and support of activists, so they are not left to face risks alone; trust in NGOs and talking to society in plain language; financial sustainability and moving beyond grant dependence; state-NGO partnership: where it is possible and where it turns into imitation; business-NGO partnership; the image of civil society in 3-5 years: what to preserve, change, and build together. The evening included an expert lounge in a live podcast format, the close of the first day, and then a group dinner and networking. Speakers Speakers at the conference included Ruslan Zakiev (Director, Diabetic Parents’ Committee DiaRKom Public Foundation), Svetlana Bogatyreva (Executive Director, Just Support private foundation), Irina Zhdanova (Chair, “My Home” Center for Development and Social Assistance to the Population), Sergey Gulyaev (Director, Desenta Foundation), Madina Tulepova (Chair, Support of Initiatives Public Association), Denis Dzhivaga (Director, Kazakhstan International Bureau for Human Rights and Rule of Law), Irina Mednikova (General Director, Youth Information Service of Kazakhstan), Aizhan Alzhanova (President, Mama Pro Foundation), Gulmira Birzhanova (Head of the Legal Service, “Media Qoldau,” Legal Media Center), and Svetlana Mogilyuk (Chair, Civil Alliance of Pavlodar Region Association). Day 2: Results and recognition The second day, 25 September, began with a presentation and discussion of the World Café results. A ceremony recognizing the contributions of project participants followed. The conference concluded with closing remarks and a group lunch. The conference combined three levels of analysis: specific stories of change, a collective diagnosis of the state of civil society, and expert reflection on values and sustainability. This structure made it possible to move from “what worked” to “why it worked,” and then to the question of “what infrastructure is needed for results to be repeatable.” Participants themselves gave the event high marks: “The conference was held at the highest level, creative and interactive.” — conference participant “I really enjoyed taking part in this event and got answers to many of my questions. I would very much like such events to be held regularly.” — conference participant This publication is funded by the European Union. Its contents are the sole responsibility of IWPR and does not necessarily reflect the views of the European Union.

https://english.news.cn/20261021/7c6ffcb.body: World Insights: China-Central Asia cooperation boosts SCO development-Xinhua World Insights: China-Central Asia cooperation boosts SCO development Source: Xinhua Editor: huaxia 2026-10-21 13:37:45 DUSHANBE, Oct. 21 (Xinhua) -- During his just-concluded official visits to Uzbekistan and Tajikistan and attendance at the 25th meeting of the Council of Heads of Government (Prime Ministers) of Member States of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO), Chinese Premier Li Qiang called for closer cooperation with the two Central Asian countries and greater development of the SCO. In recent years, China has deepened practical cooperation with Central Asian countries and injected fresh momentum into development of the SCO by enhancing connectivity, trade and exchanges in various fields. Analysts say these efforts will contribute to common prosperity and high-quality development in the region and beyond. CONNECTIVITY BRINGS OPPORTUNITY Enhancing connectivity between China and the landlocked countries of Central Asia is key to promoting development in the region and beyond. The China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway, now under construction, is a prime example of this effort. In recent years, the railway project has remained high on the agenda of leaders of the countries involved. Most recently, during Li's official visit to Uzbekistan, the two sides pledged to advance the railway's high-quality construction. The railway, launched at the end of 2024, is a flagship project of the Belt and Road Initiative, serving as a strategic link between China and Central Asia. The route will begin in Kashgar in northwest China and pass through the mountainous terrain of Kyrgyzstan to reach Uzbekistan. High-quality construction and efficient operation of the railway will set a valuable example for countries across the region and beyond, said Kubanychbek Taabaldiev, a professor at Ala-Too International University in Bishkek. "It has the potential to change the economic geography of Central Asia and transform Kyrgyzstan from a country located between major markets into an important link between China, Central Asia, and further on to European and Middle Eastern destinations," Taabaldiev said. Beyond railway and road construction, the strengthening of transport cooperation between China and Central Asian countries also encompasses facilitating customs clearance at borders, digitizing transport permits and other efficiency-enhancing measures. Better connectivity has created new development opportunities for the region, boosting trade and exchanges in various fields. Ulugbek Shermatov, chairman of the Committee on International Affairs, Defence and Security of the Legislative Chamber of the Oliy Majlis of Uzbekistan, noted that the creation of new transport arteries "not only expands economic opportunities, but also forms a solid material foundation for long-term interdependence and peaceful cooperation in the region." This demonstrates China's commitment to developing friendly relations with neighboring states and promoting Belt and Road cooperation, Shermatov said. PRACTICAL COOPERATION BEARS FRUIT From trade and agriculture to cutting-edge technological innovation, practical cooperation between China and Central Asia has been a driving force behind regional growth and, more broadly, the development of the SCO as a whole. Trade figures speak to the robust momentum in cooperation. China's trade with five Central Asian countries topped 100 billion U.S. dollars in 2025, hitting a record high. Meanwhile, trade structure continues to improve, with more Central Asian products entering the Chinese market. "Stability in the region is inextricably linked with trade and economic development. The growth of the total trade turnover of Central Asian countries with China ... clearly demonstrates China's importance in ensuring stability in our region," said Shermatov. Building on traditional merchandise trade, both sides are further expanding cooperation in digital trade, agriculture, energy, manufacturing, as well as scientific and technological innovation. Take energy cooperation as an example. Cooperation has gradually expanded from traditional oil and gas to clean energy and related technologies. At the Second China-Central Asia Summit in Astana, Kazakhstan last year, China and the five Central Asian nations pledged to support the establishment of a China-Central Asia energy development partnership to expand cooperation across the entire energy industry chains. The countries also affirmed their commitment to promoting technological and talent exchanges and cooperation in areas such as the management and development of desertified and saline-alkali lands. "China possesses rich technical expertise in renewable energy, electric mobility, digital infrastructure, telecommunications, artificial intelligence (AI) and industrial automation," said Mukhtor Umarov, chairman of the Economic Assembly of Uzbekistan. At the broader SCO level, the establishment and development of cooperation platforms between China and other SCO members in emerging fields "have opened new avenues for countries in the region -- shifting the focus from simply purchasing equipment toward technology localization, joint R&D, engineer cultivation and the buildout of new production capacities," Umarov said. SCO DEVELOPMENT STRENGTHENED Leaders of China and Central Asian nations, together with their SCO colleagues, reaffirmed stronger cooperation within the SCO framework at the just-concluded 25th meeting of the Council of Heads of Government (Prime Ministers) of Member States of the SCO in the Tajik capital of Dushanbe. China's coordination with Central Asia will help promote the high-quality development of the SCO by strengthening the foundation for regional security, expanding economic cooperation and connectivity, and cementing mutual trust among member states. These efforts will further enhance the SCO's role in safeguarding regional security, promoting common development and improving global governance, experts said. "In my view, the most prominent feature of China's current contribution to the development of the SCO lies in its tight integration of strategic concepts, multilateral rules and concrete development tools," said Uzbek expert Umarov. "Against the backdrop of intensifying geoeconomic fragmentation, increasing trade restrictions, and chronic shortages of long-term financing, SCO member states urgently need predictable rules and institutions to mitigate risks faced by enterprises," he said. China has been a key contributor to the SCO's evolution. At the Tianjin Summit last year, a milestone in the SCO's development, China and other member states jointly formulated a development strategy for the organization for the next decade and action plans to promote high-quality development. Since the Tianjin Summit, a number of cooperation platforms have been launched, covering green industry, digital economy, scientific and technological innovation, energy, education and AI. At the Bishkek Summit earlier this year, China brought more initiatives and projects supporting the SCO's development, including the establishment of a China-SCO port economic cooperation center in Tianjin, the launch of an international AI application cooperation center, and the training of more green industry professionals. The SCO's international significance is "determined not only by its geographical reach or the combined potential of its member states, but also by its ability to translate political agreements into functioning mechanisms for security, economic cooperation, and diplomatic coordination," said Guzel Maitdinova, director of the Center for Geopolitical Studies at the Russian-Tajik (Slavonic) University. "Looking ahead, linking SCO economic initiatives with national development strategies, China's Belt and Road Initiative, and the programs of international financial institutions could play a particularly important role," Maitdinova added.

https://english.news.cn/20261020/f7443db.body: Deeper China-Central Asia cooperation offers new opportunities for SCO development, says Tajik expert -Xinhua Deeper China-Central Asia cooperation offers new opportunities for SCO development, says Tajik expert Source: Xinhua Editor: huaxia 2026-10-20 23:16:15 This photo taken on Sept. 8, 2026 shows an exterior view of the pilot zone for China-SCO digital economy cooperation in Tianjin, north China. (Xinhua/Sun Fanyue) DUSHANBE, Oct. 20 (Xinhua) -- Further deepening cooperation between China and Central Asian countries will create new opportunities for the development of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO), a Tajik expert said. In recent years, China and Central Asian countries have strengthened cooperation and achieved fruitful results in a number of areas, said Guzel Maitdinova, director of the Center for Geopolitical Studies at the Russian-Tajik (Slavonic) University, in a recent interview with Xinhua. One of the key indicators of these achievements is the growth in trade volume between China and the five Central Asian countries -- Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, Kyrgyzstan and Turkmenistan, which exceeded 100 billion U.S. dollars in 2025 for the first time, Maitdinova noted. Furthermore, regular political dialogue has been established, transport connectivity has expanded, industrial and technological cooperation has developed, and environmental and humanitarian issues have become part of the shared agenda, she added. "For the SCO, deeper China-Central Asia ties create opportunities to broaden the organization's cooperation agenda by linking security with economic development, digital transformation, energy, environmental sustainability and human capital development," the expert said. A drone photo taken on Aug. 15, 2026 shows workers at a construction site of a grand bridge above the Kec-Alat River along the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway in Jalalabad, Kyrgyzstan. (Xinhua/Li Renzi) Maitdinova cited Chinese President Xi Jinping's remarks at the SCO summit in Bishkek in September, where he described the organization as "a priority area for promoting high-quality Belt and Road cooperation and implementing the Global Development Initiative." She said the SCO provides a political and institutional platform for coordinating interests, while the Belt and Road Initiative promotes cooperation through infrastructure projects, investment and trade. Together, they create opportunities to develop cross-border transport corridors, energy networks, digital infrastructure and production chains. Amid profound changes in the international landscape, the SCO is playing an increasingly important role in coordinating interests across Eurasia and advancing multilateral diplomacy, Maitdinova said. At the Bishkek summit, Xi called for putting development first, taking security as a key goal, adopting a people-centered approach and promoting dialogue and consultation. "These priorities reflect the SCO's role in strengthening regional security, promoting economic connectivity and maintaining dialogue among countries with different political and economic priorities," she said. Students try making mooncakes at the Confucius Institute at the Tashkent State University of Oriental Studies in Tashkent, Uzbekistan, Sept. 24, 2026. (Xinhua/Bao Nuomin) This year marks the 25th anniversary of the founding of the SCO. As Maitdinova pointed out, over the past quarter-century, the organization has developed a multilayered system of intergovernmental cooperation in which security issues are addressed in conjunction with economic development and people-to-people exchanges. In her view, amid profound changes in the international situation, the SCO has evolved not only into a platform for regional dialogue and security coordination, but also into a significant mechanism for reconciling the interests of states in the emerging multipolar world order. Maitdinova described the "Shanghai Spirit" as both the guiding principle of the SCO and a distinctive model of intergovernmental relations that emerged as countries in the region sought new mechanisms for security and cooperation. The Shanghai Spirit embodies six principles -- mutual trust, mutual benefit, equality, consultation, respect for diversity of civilizations, and pursuit of common development. These principles provide a basis for cooperation among countries with different political systems, levels of economic development and foreign policy priorities, Maitdinova said. Guided by the Shanghai Spirit, the SCO continues to develop and strengthen, helping translate multilateral dialogue into concrete results in cooperation among member states, she added. ■ You may like In pics: 2026 Beijing China Art International Fair Swans seen on Ganhe River in Jiagedaqi, China's Heilongjiang Ancient ethnic village in Yunnan thrives on cultural tourism Autumn scenery at Xixiasong scenic area in China's Gansu Young entrepreneurs make Yunnan flowers more flourishing China's manned deep-sea submersible completes 470th dive More from GLOBALink 90 years after Liangzhu's discovery, a lost city and a civilization brought back to life The secret a town kept for the Red Army | Long March stories Inside China's "unlikely" AI computing hub

https://omik.osce.org/news/mission-kosov.body: News News Item OSCE report finds progress and gaps in handling organised crime and corruption cases in Kosovo Issued on: 21 October 2026 Issued by: OSCE Mission in Kosovo PRISHTINË/PRIŠTINA, 21 October 2026 - Judicial institutions in Kosovo have taken important steps to strengthen the handling of serious organized crime and corruption cases, but reforms have yet to translate into consistent courtroom practice, according to the OSCE’s second Regional Trial Monitoring Report, published today. The report, part of a wider OSCE trial monitoring programme in the region funded by the EU, examines developments across six Western Balkan jurisdictions since 2024 when last recommendations were issued. It assesses progress in their implementation and identifies practical priorities for fairer, more efficient and effective criminal justice system. Drawing on courtroom monitoring, analysis of judicial decisions and consultations with judicial institutions, it finds stronger institutional ownership of reforms, including strategic planning, expanded digital tools, specialized training and measures to promote more consistent judicial practice. Improved publication of judicial decisions is one example of progress. During the reporting period, 36 of 41 monitored judgments were published online, including all 20 monitored Court of Appeals judgments. Institutions have also taken steps to strengthen interpretation and translation services and improve communication with the public. Nevertheless, implementation remains uneven. The report identifies continuing challenges related to lengthy proceedings, particularly at the appellate level; consistency in indictment drafting and judicial reasoning; access to interpretation and translated case materials; and the use of financial investigations, confiscation and accessory punishments. “The report recognises the progress made by justice institutions and their follow up to our recommendations. The next step is to build on this progress so that reforms consistently improve how complex cases are prepared, managed and decided,” said Kahramon Sanginov, Project Manager for the Kosovo component. Its recommendations call for clearer institutional responsibilities, stronger follow-up and sustained investment in specialised expertise and operational resources. The emphasis is on ensuring that strategies, guidance and digital tools produce measurable improvements in everyday case handling, while safeguarding fair trial rights and judicial independence. The findings and recommendations will be discussed at the Regional Judicial Forum in Budva, Montenegro, on 26–27 October 2026. The Forum will bring together senior judicial and prosecutorial representatives from all project jurisdictions to exchange practical experience on turning justice reforms into sustained institutional practice. Full report is available here . Factsheet with key takeaways here . https://montenegro.osce.org/news/mission.body: News News Item New report highlights progress and priorities for Montenegro’s justice system Issued on: 21 October 2026 Issued by: OSCE Mission to Montenegro Fields of work: Rule of law Podgorica, 21 October 2026 – Over the past two years, Montenegro has strengthened its framework for tackling serious organized crime and corruption cases. Findings from the OSCE Mission to Montenegro’s trial monitoring work suggest that the next step is to ensure these reforms translate into sustained implementation. These findings are part of the second report from the OSCE’s Regional Trial Monitoring Project – Combatting Organised Crime and Corruption in the Western Balkans , published today. Over the past two years, the Mission’s Trial Monitoring team monitored 1,018 hearings in 61 cases and held nearly 100 meetings and consultations with justice sector stakeholders. Their findings point to progress across Montenegro’s justice system while identifying areas where further improvements can be made. Among the key developments identified in the report is a more focused mandate for the Special State Prosecutor’s Office (SPO) and the Specialized Department of the High Court in Podgorica, enabling both institutions to concentrate on the most complex organized crime and corruption cases. The report also notes new binding instructions on financial investigations, stronger safeguards for prosecutorial autonomy, and Supreme Court efforts to harmonize judicial practice, particularly in money laundering cases. Guidelines on criminal sanctions and trial management, alongside more direct communication between the Judicial Council, courts and judges, have also supported improvements in practice. Further support for these efforts includes specialized training provided by the Centre for Training in the Judiciary and State Prosecution Service, as well as improved appraisal systems for judges and prosecutors. The report nonetheless notes that progress should be accompanied by sustained implementation. Priorities identified in the report include further improvements in the efficiency of complex cases, more final judgements, and stronger permanent confiscation of assets derived from criminal activity. Other areas requiring further attention include improving the premises of the Specialized Department of the High Court in Podgorica, raising the quality of prosecutorial and judicial acts, and strengthening transparency and safeguards against undue external influence. Welcoming the report’s publication, the Head of the OSCE Mission to Montenegro, Ambassador Jan Haukaas, highlighted the uptake of the Project’s recommendations by Montenegrin justice institutions as a constructive contribution to reform. “The Project’s recommendations have helped shape the justice system’s strategic priorities, with many already implemented or underway. This demonstrates that independent trial monitoring, combined with open dialogue and institutional commitment, can contribute to positive change,” stated Ambassador Haukaas. https://daryo.uz/en/2026/10/20/number-of.body: Uzbekistan Number of Uzbek citizens going to Russia for work falls 13.2% The number of Uzbek citizens going to Russia for work fell 13.2% year-on-year to 1.179mn in the first half of 2026, while labor migration to the European Union, Türkiye and South Korea continued to grow and remittances from Russia increased by 8.8%. Yesterday, 16:00 1 min read 3 716 views 0 comments 0 Source: “Daryo” / Farrux Aliyev The number of Uzbek citizens who went to Russia for work fell by 13.2% year-on-year in January-June 2026, reaching 1.179mn, according to the Central Bank of Uzbekistan’s Labor Market Review . The figure compares with 1.358mn in the first half of 2025. For comparison, the report recorded 1.495mn Uzbek citizens working in Russia under a patent in 2025. Meanwhile, Uzbekistan’s external labor migration is increasingly extending to other destinations. In 2025, the number of Uzbek migrant workers in the European Union rose by 13.2%, while the number in Türkiye increased by 10.7%, the Central Bank reported. As of July 1, 2026, the number of Uzbek citizens in Türkiye reached 70,000, up 9.3% year-on-year. South Korea registered 102,200 Uzbek citizens, an annual increase of 3.3%. Despite the decline in the number of Uzbek citizens going to Russia for work, remittance inflows from the country continued to grow. Transfers from Russia to Uzbekistan increased by 8.8% year-on-year in the first half of 2026. The Central Bank warned that declining labor migration to some destinations could negatively affect future remittance inflows, household incomes and consumer demand. The report also highlighted a weakening domestic labor market. The number of job vacancies announced in the second quarter of 2026 fell by 9.8%, while job-seeker activity remained high and competition for available positions intensified, as previously reported by Daryo. # Domestic Labor Market # central bank of uzbekistan # labor migration # remittances # russia # uzbekistan Telegram channel @daryo_eng Subscribe What do you think? Читайте также: Плата за электроэнергию. Сравниваем наши счета с другими странами (и с доходами) Он отметил, что война на Ближнем Востоке наносит региону крайне неравномерный экономический удар. Экономики, непосредственно затронутые конфликтом, находятся под сильным давлением, в то время как другие экономики стран Ближнего Востока, Северной Африки, Афганистана и Пакистана (MENAP), а также большая часть стран Кавказа и Центральной Азии (CCA) продемонстрировали большую устойчивость. Перспективы критически зависят от того, насколько быстро нормализуются производство энергоносителей и торговля, а также от способности стран сохранять макроэкономическую стабильность. директор департамента Ближнего Востока и Центральной Азии МВФ Джихад Азур Джихад Азур напомнил, что добыча нефти почти у всех непосредственно пострадавших экспортеров резко сократилась, а сбои в судоходстве и переработке привели к резкому росту цен на топливо. Тем не менее воздействие оказалось более сдержанным, чем предполагалось изначально. Довоенные излишки, добыча нефти производителями, не входящими в страны Персидского залива, альтернативные транспортные маршруты, корректировка спроса и существенное сокращение запасов - все это помогло смягчить удар. "Эти резервы дали время, но они конечны. Запасы ниже, резервные мощности ограничены, а возобновление сбоев может привести к гораздо большей корректировке цен", - считает он. Чего ждать Кавказу и Центральной Азии В МВФ подчеркивают, что регион Кавказа и Центральной Азии относительно успешно справился с потрясением благодаря значительному объему денежных переводов и высокой инвестиционной активности. Ожидается, что темпы роста замедлятся с 6,2% в 2025 году до более устойчивого уровня в 5,2% в 2026 году и 5,0% в 2027 году. Ожидается, что инфляция продолжит снижаться с высоких уровней, хотя и разными темпами в разных странах региона, в зависимости в том числе от проводимой ими экономической политики. Этот прогноз сопряжен с исключительно высокой степенью неопределенности. директор департамента Ближнего Востока и Центральной Азии МВФ Джихад Азур Наиболее серьезным риском является затягивание конфликта на Ближнем Востоке. Дальнейшие перебои в добыче энергоносителей, работе транспортных маршрутов или функционировании критически важной инфраструктуры ослабят экономическую активность в странах Персидского залива - экспортерах нефти, а также усилят инфляционное давление и создадут дополнительную нагрузку на бюджетную и внешнеэкономическую сферы стран региона. Кроме того, ужесточение глобальных финансовых условий может привести к ослаблению спроса, росту стоимости заимствований, усилению давления на валютные курсы и усугублению уязвимости экономик, нуждающихся в значительных объемах государственного финансирования или зависящих от внешних источников средств. Читайте также: Кыргызстану предрекли роль лидера по росту цен в Центральной Азии. Прогноз МВФ "Особо уязвимыми остаются страны с низким уровнем дохода и нестабильные экономики. Высокая зависимость от импорта продовольствия и ограниченные возможности бюджетного маневра на фоне сокращения официальной помощи в целях развития лишают многие из этих стран достаточного запаса прочности для преодоления потрясений", - считает директор департамента Ближнего Востока и Центральной Азии МВФ. Напомним, по прогнозу МВФ, Кыргызстан будет лидером не только по росту экономики, но и по инфляции . Ожидается, что по итогам 2026 года рост цен в нашей стране составит 12,7%, а в 2027 году он ускорится до 14,3%. При этом в среднем по региону Кавказа и Центральной Азии инфляция ожидается на уровне 13% и 10,2%. "Полный текст доклада "Региональные экономические перспективы" будет опубликован 22 октября в Дубае. В нем мы представим более подробную оценку экономических событий и приоритетных направлений политики в масштабах всего региона", - сказал Джихад Азур. Как органам власти следует реагировать на вызовы Джихад Азур отметил, что рекомендации МВФ сосредоточены на трех ключевых направлениях. В первую очередь, приоритетом для органов власти должно оставаться обеспечение ценовой стабильности при одновременном поддержании бюджетной устойчивости. Читайте также: ЕФСР улучшил прогноз по росту ВВП КР в 2026 году. Но предупредил о замедлении экономики "В случае возникновения инфляционного давления первой линией защиты должна служить денежно-кредитная политика. Меры по ужесточению денежно-кредитной политики и ограничению ликвидности необходимо подкреплять взвешенной бюджетной политикой, особенно в странах с ограниченными возможностями бюджетного маневра", - сказал представитель МВФ. Он также отметил, что создание резервов бюджета остается крайне важной задачей для всего региона, учитывая сохраняющиеся риски ухудшения экономической ситуации. Возможные меры политики могут включать более эффективную мобилизацию внутренних доходов, рационализацию расходов и укрепление основ бюджетной политики. Читайте также: Доходы кыргызстанцев не успевают за ценами. Цифры Органам власти следует воздерживаться от введения субсидий широкого охвата и вместо этого сосредоточиться на поддержке наиболее уязвимых групп населения посредством адресных, временных и бюджетно-нейтральных денежных выплат. директор департамента Ближнего Востока и Центральной Азии МВФ Джихад Азур В-третьих, странам необходимо продолжать наращивать потенциал для противодействия будущим потрясениям . Подчеркивается, что недавний опыт подтверждает важность надежных основ экономической политики. Страны с сильными институтами, заслуживающими доверия механизмами денежно-кредитной политики (обеспечиваемыми независимостью центральных банков) и достаточным пространством для бюджетного маневра, как правило, лучше подготовлены к преодолению потрясений. Читайте также: Скоро зима. Каким будет отопительный сезон (неутешительные прогнозы) "Диверсификация торговли, углубление региональной интеграции и расширение возможностей для внедрения новых технологий, включая искусственный интеллект, могут способствовать росту производительности и долгосрочному экономическому развитию. Это особенно актуально, когда данные меры подкрепляются реформами, направленными на повышение конкурентоспособности", - отметил Джихад Азур. Читайте также: В Налоговый кодекс вносят очередные изменения. Рассказываем о самых главных Директор департамента Ближнего Востока и Центральной Азии МВФ также обратил внимание на то, что потенциал Среднего коридора и расширение торговли с Китаем, Европой и Ближним Востоком открывают перед странами Кавказа и Центральной Азии широкие возможности для углубления интеграции в мировую экономику. Он напомнил, что страны региона уже активно инвестируют в развитие инфраструктуры, хотя этот процесс требует времени. ВВП аналитика прогноз МВФ Есть новость или проблема? https://kz.kursiv.media/en/2026-10-21/en.body: Photo: Kaztransoil.kz, photo editor: Dastan Shanay Oil exports through the Atasu-Alashankou pipeline rose 26% year-on-year to 983,000 tons in January-September, KazTransOil, Kazakhstan’s national oil pipeline operator and a subsidiary of KazMunayGas, said. Kazakhstan-China Pipeline LLP transported 14.8 million tons of oil through its main pipeline system in the first nine months of 2026, up 2% year-on-year. Most of the volume was transited through Kazakhstan to China. Meanwhile, exports of Kazakh oil to China rose 26%. «A total of 8.517 million tons of oil was transported via the Atasu-Alashankou pipeline, an increase of 255,000 tons compared with the same period last year. Of this volume, 983,000 tons were designated for export, up 26% compared with the first nine months of 2025. Transit volumes amounted to 7.533 million tons,» the company said in a release. Kazakhstan-China Pipeline LLP operates the Atasu-Alashankou and Kenkiyak-Kumkol pipelines. KazTransOil and China National Oil and Gas Exploration and Development Company Ltd. (CNODC) each own a 50% stake in the company. In December 2012, shares representing 10% of KazTransOil minus one ordinary share were offered on the Kazakhstan Stock Exchange (KASE) under the People’s IPO program at 725 tenge per share. Kursiv.media previously reported that Kazakhstan aims to fully meet domestic fuel demand and begin exporting finished petroleum products to Central Asian countries by 2030. https://asiaplus.news/en/2026/10/21/huma.body: Share Payrav Chorshanbiev , asia+ Categories Society Tajikistan Format News Published 21.10.2026 09:36 Tajikistan received more than 8,901 tons of humanitarian aid worth $25.3 million from 38 countries in January–September 2026, down $21.8 million, or 46.3%, from the same period last year, according to the Customs Service under the Government of Tajikistan. Russia accounted for the largest share of humanitarian aid during the first nine months of 2026, providing 29.2% of the total value. The United States ranked second with 20.3%, followed by China with 10.8%, the Netherlands with 8.2%, India with 8.1%, South Korea with 6.4%, Belgium with 5.1%, Iran with 2.5% and Japan with 1.6%. Other donor countries included Germany, Türkiye, Denmark, Finland, Belarus, the United Arab Emirates, Italy, the United Kingdom, Australia, Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan. The donor structure has changed significantly over the past year. In January–September 2025, China was Tajikistan’s largest humanitarian aid donor, accounting for 33.7% of the total, followed by the United States at 24%. Russia contributed just 6.5%. Russia’s share has since increased more than fourfold, from 6.5% to 29.2%, while China’s share has fallen from 33.7% to 10.8%. In monetary terms, humanitarian aid from China declined from approximately $15.9 million in the first nine months of 2025 to $2.7 million in the same period this year. Meanwhile, aid from Russia rose from $3.1 million to $7.4 million. Aid deliveries fluctuate throughout the year Monthly figures published by the Agency on Statistics show that humanitarian aid deliveries varied considerably during the first nine months of 2026. In January, aid worth approximately $435,400 entered the country. Deliveries increased sharply in February, reaching around $5 million, followed by a further $2.9 million in March. Inflows were comparatively modest in April and May, with May’s total amounting to approximately $290,000. The highest monthly figure was recorded in July, when humanitarian aid worth $5.5 million arrived in Tajikistan. Deliveries remained substantial in August, at around $3 million, and September, at $4.3 million. February, July and September together accounted for more than half of the total value of humanitarian aid received during the nine-month period. Who receives the humanitarian aid? Humanitarian cargo can include food, medicines, medical equipment and other goods intended to support the population and social institutions. One example is Russian assistance intended to provide schoolchildren with hot meals. However, publicly available official statistics do not provide a comprehensive picture of how humanitarian aid entering Tajikistan is distributed or who ultimately receives it. The Agency for Statistics publishes data on the total value and weight of humanitarian cargo and identifies donor countries. However, its publicly available reports do not detail the types of goods received or their distribution among regions, institutions and population groups. Government bodies, including the Agency for State Material Reserves, do not provide media outlets with comprehensive information on the distribution of incoming humanitarian cargo. Information about recipients is therefore mainly available through individual reports announcing the handover of aid. While official figures make it possible to assess the overall scale of deliveries and the contributions of individual donor countries, they do not reveal the full picture of who benefits from the assistance or in what quantities. The statistical publications also do not explain the reasons for the 46.3% decline in the value of humanitarian aid recorded in January–September 2026 compared with the same period last year. The figures reflect the value and weight of humanitarian cargo recorded by the Customs Service. They do not cover all forms of international assistance to Tajikistan, including financial support, grants and technical assistance. Join us on social media! Once fully operational, it will reduce border crossing time to just 10 seconds. Overall, Khorgos has launched around 50 new tourism projects so far. https://en.kabar.kg/news/kyrgyzstan-chin.body: Jogorku Kenesh Bishkek, Oct. 21, 2026 /Kabar/. On October 20, Elvira Surabaldieva, Chair of the Committee on International Affairs, Defense, Security, and Migration of the Jogorku Kenesh (Parliament of Kyrgyzstan) met with a delegation from the Foreign Affairs Committee of the Chinese People’s Political Consultative Conference (CPPCC) of the Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region (XUAR), led by Director Zhang Huazhong. Cholpon Esenamanova, Deputy Chair of the Committee, also participated in the meeting. The parties discussed current issues regarding Kyrgyz-Chinese cooperation, with a particular focus on developing inter-parliamentary ties, as well as trade, economic, cultural, and humanitarian engagement. Elvira Surabaldieva emphasized that Kyrgyzstan attaches great importance to strengthening friendly relations with China and developing a comprehensive strategic partnership. She noted that agreements reached at the highest level provide a foundation for further deepening bilateral cooperation and implementing joint projects. The Committee Chair highlighted the importance of intensifying dialogue between the Jogorku Kenesh and the CPPCC of the XUAR, exchanging delegations and expertise, and strengthening interaction between relevant specialized bodies. Special attention was also given to prospects for expanding trade and economic ties and attracting investment. In this context, Elvira Surabaldieva emphasized the strategic importance of constructing the China–Kyrgyzstan–Uzbekistan railway, developing road transport links along the Barskoon–Bedel route, and ensuring the efficient operation of border crossing points on the Kyrgyz–Chinese border. Furthermore, the parties explored the possibilities of increasing the number of direct flights between Kyrgyzstan and China, including the launch of a Kashgar–Bishkek route, as well as establishing logistics centers and developing e-commerce. For his part, Zhang Huazhong reaffirmed a commitment to further developing mutually beneficial cooperation and strengthening ties between Kyrgyzstan and the Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region (XUAR) of the PRC. He expressed confidence that constructive dialogue and joint efforts would facilitate the implementation of the agreements reached and further strengthen the Kyrgyz–Chinese partnership. Print

Shipping Azerbaijan News 21 October 2026 13:51 (UTC +04:00) Photo: Trend News Agency Aytaj Shiraliyeva Economics Journalist Read more BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 21. A terminal should be built in Turkmenbashi to facilitate container transit from China through Turkmenistan, the Deputy Chairman of the Association of Freight Forwarders of Azerbaijan and General Director of U.F.E. Shipping, Elmir Poladov, said at the EU-Azerbaijan Business Forum in Baku on Wednesday, Trend ’s correspondent reports from the event. According to him, the falling level of the Caspian Sea requires more comprehensive measures than port dredging, as dredging works will have to be carried out regularly if the water level continues to decline. He noted that the level of the Caspian Sea largely depends on the volume of water flowing into it from the Volga River, which is decreasing. "The seabed can be deepened by several meters or even five meters every year, but the water level will fall again the following year, requiring dredging works to be carried out repeatedly," he explained. Poladov also highlighted Turkmenistan's potential for developing transportation along the Middle Corridor. According to him, the country has a sufficiently large and well-equipped port. However, several issues need to be resolved to organize container transportation from China to Azerbaijan through Turkmenistan. In particular, he pointed to the need to build a container terminal at the port of Turkmenbashi and establish a feeder shipping connection between Turkmenbashi and Alat. Poladov expressed hope that the implementation of existing projects would enable container cargo to be transported from China to Azerbaijan through Turkmenistan. Meanwhile, the EU-Azerbaijan Business Forum is taking place in Baku, marking the 30th anniversary of the partnership between the European Union and Azerbaijan, as well as the 10th anniversary of the forum. This year's event is being held under the theme "Bridging Corridors: Connectivity & Infrastructure." The main focus is on developing transport connectivity and infrastructure, strengthening economic cooperation between the EU and Azerbaijan, and expanding regional trade and investment. The forum's program includes high-level discussions, thematic sessions, and business meetings involving representatives from the public and private sectors. https://www.trend.az/casia/kazakhstan/42.body: Home Central Asia Kazakhstan Tokayev, CNMC chairman discuss Kazakhstan-China copper smelter project Kazakhstan News 20 October 2026 18:04 (UTC +04:00) Photo: Akorda Alyona Pavlenko Journalist, International Desk Read more BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 20. Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev met with China Nonferrous Metal Mining Group (CNMC) Chairman Wen Gang after launching construction of the Aktogay copper smelter in the Abai region via video link, according to the Kazakh presidential press service. Tokayev highlighted CNMC's international experience in mining and metallurgy and its contribution to developing Kazakhstan's industrial capacity. He said the project would give additional impetus to economic development in the Abai region and Kazakhstan's manufacturing industry. Wen Gang thanked Tokayev for his trust in CNMC to implement the project and for taking part in the construction launch ceremony. He assured the president that the company would carry out construction using advanced technologies and within the established timeframe, with particular attention to industrial and environmental safety. Wen Gang said the project would also expand cooperation in local workforce training and the exchange of expertise. The two sides noted that the project would serve as an example of industrial cooperation between Kazakhstan and China and provide a basis for further joint work in metallurgy and deeper processing. Earlier today, Tokayev launched construction of the Aktogay copper smelter via video link. The plant, being developed by KAZ Minerals Group with China's NFC as the engineering partner, will have an annual capacity of 300,000 tons of cathode copper. The first copper cathode is scheduled to be produced in 2030, and the project is expected to create more than 1,000 jobs. https://www.azernews.az/region/265942.ht.body: Russia-led bloc says Armenia would pay steep price for EU pivot 21 October 2026 14:31 (UTC+04:00) Akbar Novruz Read more A report prepared by four members of the Russia-led Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU) has warned that Armenia could face severe economic consequences if it leaves the bloc to pursue European Union membership, while the impact on the remaining member states would be minimal. Russia, Belarus, Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan have presented a report exceeding 70 pages examining the potential consequences of Armenia's withdrawal from the EAEU and its possible accession to the European Union. According to the report, Armenia would experience substantial economic losses from abandoning the Eurasian integration framework, whereas the economic consequences for the other four members would be comparatively insignificant. The assessment comes amid growing disagreements between Yerevan and its EAEU partners over Armenia's efforts to deepen political and economic relations with the European Union. The four member states have also requested an additional report, to be prepared by December, examining the potential implications of suspending Armenia's participation in the organisation. Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan, however, has rejected suggestions that his government has breached its commitments to the EAEU. He maintained that Armenia continues to fulfil its obligations under the bloc's agreements and has not taken a decision to withdraw from the organisation. Armenia joined the EAEU in 2015, becoming part of the economic integration framework alongside Russia, Belarus, Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan. However, relations between Yerevan and its traditional partners have become increasingly complicated as Armenia seeks closer integration with European institutions. In 2025, the Armenian Parliament adopted legislation initiating the country's EU accession process, marking a significant step in Yerevan's efforts to strengthen ties with Brussels. The move drew criticism from Moscow and Minsk, which argue that full membership in the European Union is incompatible with continued participation in the EAEU because of conflicting customs and trade obligations. Despite the legislation, Armenia has not formally withdrawn from the Eurasian Economic Union, and the adoption of the law does not itself constitute EU membership or the formal opening of accession negotiations. The latest report highlights the widening disagreement between Armenia and its EAEU partners over the country's future economic alignment. While the four member states portray a potential Armenian withdrawal as economically damaging primarily to Yerevan, the Armenian government maintains that it has not made a final decision to leave the bloc. He highlighted the importance of the agreements reached between the two countries, including the Treaty on Allied Relations signed during Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev’s state visit to Kyrgyzstan in July this year, for the further development of bilateral ties. For her part, Gafarova conveyed President Aliyev’s greetings and best wishes to Japarov. The speaker noted the dynamic development of bilateral relations, including interparliamentary cooperation, and stressed the importance of further strengthening ties between the two countries. The meeting also addressed prospects for expanding Kyrgyz-Azerbaijani cooperation in various fields, including trade and economic relations, investment, energy and transport. https://www.cacianalyst.org/publications.body: Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan and China Coordinate Logistics Along The Middle Corridor Tuesday, 20 October 2026 Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan and China Coordinate Logistics Along The Middle Corridor Featured Published in Analytical Articles font size decrease font size increase font size Print Email By: Vusal Guliyev Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, and China increasingly seek to strengthen the Middle Corridor as a trans-Eurasian trade and logistics route. China’s proposal to extend Lianyungang Port’s existing logistics chain to Baku, alongside expanding container capacity at Aktau and new multimodal transport agreements, reflects a shift toward integrating previously separate infrastructure projects. Building on the existing Lianyungang–Khorgos–Aktau “Three Nodes” logistics chain, the proposed extension to Baku could further integrate transport networks across China, Central Asia, and the South Caucasus, strengthening freight connectivity with European markets. It could also create opportunities for Japan and South Korea to diversify their trade and energy routes amid disruptions to traditional supply chains. However, its long-term viability will depend on whether the participating countries can coordinate railway services, port operations, customs procedures, and digital systems to deliver reliable, cost-effective, and commercially competitive freight services. BACKGROUND: On September 9, 2026, Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev’s interview with Xinhua highlighted the growing importance of the Azerbaijan–Kazakhstan-China logistics connection. The same day in Baku, at the CICA Conference of Port Authorities, Jiang Wei, Vice President for External Relations of Lianyungang Port, proposed incorporating Baku into the existing Lianyungang–Khorgos–Aktau “Three Nodes” logistics chain. At the sidelines of the conference, Rovshan Rustamov, Chairman of Azerbaijan Railways (ADY), met with representatives of China’s Shanghai International Port Group (SIPG), NIZE Tech, and Lianyungang Port. Discussions focused on developing the Lianyungang–Baku route, expanding regular container and block-train services, attracting additional Chinese cargo bound for Europe, and introducing smart-port technologies and digital solutions. The participants also highlighted the importance of exchanging information on cargo forecasts, train schedules, and logistical requirements to improve coordination between railway and port operations and strengthen the Middle Corridor’s competitiveness. On September 8, Tahir Budagov, Deputy Chairman of Azerbaijan’s ruling New Azerbaijan Party (YAP), met with a Chinese delegation led by Liu Haixing, Minister of the International Department of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee. Their discussions focused on trade, transportation, the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI), the Zangezur Corridor, and Beijing’s support for Azerbaijan’s deeper engagement with the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO). These developments build on a growing network of infrastructure investments and bilateral agreements established in previous years, supported by sustained high-level engagement among the participating governments. On July 3, 2024, Azerbaijan and China adopted a Joint Declaration on the Establishment of a Strategic Partnership in Astana. The declaration committed both countries to strengthening cooperation on the Middle Corridor and accelerating the development of China–Europe freight-train services. That same day, KTZ Express, Aktau International Commercial Sea Port, and Lianyungang Port Group reached an agreement on the key terms for establishing a joint venture to develop a container hub at Aktau Port. The US$ 96 million project envisaged the construction, management, and operation of a new container terminal with a planned annual capacity of 500,000 TEUs (twenty-foot equivalent unit). In September 2024, Lianyungang Port Group Co., Ltd., Kazakhstan Express Rail Company, and Aktau International Commercial Sea Port signed agreements to implement the Aktau Port Container Hub project. The facility officially began operations on June 9, 2025, strengthening Kazakhstan’s transit capacity along the Trans-Caspian International Transport Route. Meanwhile, in November 2024, during COP29 in Baku, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, and China’s Xi’an Free Trade Port Construction and Operation Co., Ltd. agreed to establish a joint venture to develop an intermodal cargo terminal on an initial 40-hectare site at the Port of Baku in Alat. In April 2025, the transport ministers of Azerbaijan and China inked the Agreement on International Multimodal Transportation in Beijing. In July 2025, Azerbaijan Railways (ADY) concluded separate agreements with China State Railway Group and Xi’an Free Trade Port to strengthen the Baku–Tbilisi–Kars railway, expand rail transit, and establish a container yard at Xi’an with an annual handling capacity of 20,000 TEUs. These joint initiatives establish the foundations for a logistics network connecting Chinese inland and coastal transport hubs with Kazakhstan’s railways and Caspian ports, Azerbaijan’s transport infrastructure, and onward routes to Europe. IMPLICATIONS: The proposed extension of the Lianyungang–Khorgos–Aktau chain to Baku represents a shift from developing individual transport projects toward coordinating a broader logistics network. The initiative seeks to connect existing facilities through more integrated freight services and information systems. Azerbaijan’s greater integration into the trans-Eurasian maritime network could strengthen China’s connectivity with markets west of the Caspian Sea and improve links between its inland logistics centers and European destinations. With an annual cargo throughput of 367 million tons and 7.1598 million TEUs, Lianyungang Port serves as a key transit gateway connecting China’s maritime trade routes with its inland transport networks, while Khorgos facilitates cross-border rail connectivity between China and the wider Caspian–Central Asia region. Aktau provides access to the Caspian Sea, while Baku serves as a gateway to the South Caucasus and onward transport routes through Georgia and Türkiye. With a planned annual cargo-handling capacity of 25 million tons, the Port of Baku is positioned to play a vital role in strengthening Eurasian connectivity. Closer integration with the Lianyungang–Khorgos–Aktau network could reinforce Azerbaijan’s strategic importance in the trans-Caspian trade and logistics ecosystem. Closer coordination with Baku is also enabling Astana to better leverage its Caspian logistics infrastructure and reinforce its position along westbound trade routes. To expand the Middle Corridor’s capacity, Kazakhstan plans to increase the combined cargo-handling capacity of the Aktau and Kuryk ports from 21 million to 30 million tons through modernization efforts. Authorities in Azerbaijan and Kazakhstan have been working to improve trans-Caspian freight transport along the Baku–Aktau route. As part of these efforts, an electronic data exchange system was introduced between the two ports in April 2025 to enhance inter-port coordination, streamline cargo operations, and improve freight efficiency across the Caspian basin. Moreover, given the proximity of Lianyungang Port to major maritime hubs in Japan and South Korea, the Lianyungang–Khorgos–Aktau–Baku logistics chain could provide both countries with an additional trade route into the wider Caspian-Central Asian region. Amid escalating geopolitical tensions, sanctions-related constraints, and disruptions linked to the war in Ukraine and the ongoing conflict in the Persian Gulf, the Middle Corridor is gaining prominence as a potentially more resilient supply channel for both countries. Tokyo and Seoul have already expanded their engagement with Central Asia through multilateral cooperation frameworks that strongly support their involvement in the Middle Corridor’s development. https://www.trend.az/casia/uzbekistan/42.body: Home Central Asia Uzbekistan Uzbekneftegaz, China's CNPC seek to accelerate joint oil and gas projects Uzbekistan News 21 October 2026 09:55 (UTC +04:00) Photo: Uzbekneftegaz Niljan Bakhshaliyeva Uzbekistan Economics Correspondent Read more BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 21. Uzbekistan’s state-owned oil and gas company Uzbekneftegaz and China National Petroleum Corporation (CNPC) have discussed expanding cooperation in oil and gas exploration, drilling, production efficiency and fuel supplies during a meeting in Tashkent on October 20. This was reflected in the statement by the Uzbekneftegaz, following a meeting between Uzbekneftegaz Chairman Abdugani Sanginov and a CNPC delegation led by company President Zhou Xinhuai to review ongoing projects, accelerate joint initiatives and explore new areas of cooperation. The sides reviewed joint work in drilling, geological exploration, seismic surveys, improving gas recovery rates at fields, digitalization, engineering and the supply of modern equipment. Projects involving CNPC subsidiaries Xibu, BGP, CCDC and CNLC were highlighted as contributing to the development of Uzbekistan’s technological capabilities in the oil and gas sector. In addition, the meeting focused on efforts to address the consequences of an accident at the M-25 field. The project includes plans to drill rescue wells as part of the response, according to the statement. The sides also discussed diversifying sources of petroleum product supplies to ensure stable fuel availability in Uzbekistan’s domestic market. They expressed readiness to develop long-term supply mechanisms and improve coordination between the relevant companies. As cooperation expands, the parties considered establishing a permanent CNPC representative office in Tashkent and developing administrative infrastructure to coordinate joint projects. Moreover, they discussed opportunities to support social initiatives. The talks included support for the Tashkent branch of Gubkin Russian State University of Oil and Gas, with a focus on training qualified engineering and technical specialists to meet the needs of Uzbekistan’s oil and gas industry and future projects. The sides reaffirmed their commitment to deepening the partnership, introducing new technological solutions and advancing joint initiatives toward practical implementation. https://kaktus.media/doc/555424_kyrgyzst.body: kaktus.media Кыргызстан продлевает запрет на ввоз кузовов автомобилей Экономика 386 21 октября 2026 12:30 Kaktus Все самое интересное в Telegram Кабинет министров КР предлагает продлить временный запрет на импорт кузовов легковых автомобилей на шесть месяцев. Мера направлена против "конструкторов" - машин, которые собирают из ввезенных частей без нормального таможенного оформления и потом легализуют. Проект документа опубликован для общественного обсуждения. Что предлагается? Во исполнение указа президента о легализации автотранспорта от 31 декабря 2024 года был введен временный запрет на ввоз кузовов автомобилей, который регулярно продлевали. Очередной был продлен в апреле и действует до конца октября. Предлагается продлить эту меру еще на полгода. Запрет касается кузовов легковых автомобилей категории M1. Сейчас кузовную сборку ведут несколько предприятий, в том числе "ДТ Техник", "Шумкар", "Кыргыз Унаа Курулуш", "Меридиан Голд" и "Белес Групп". Для них предлагается сделать исключение. Для чего это делается? Основная цель - остановить практику сборки так называемых конструкторов. Такие машины собирают на территории Кыргызстана из ввезенных кузовов, агрегатов и запчастей, часто без полного таможенного оформления. При регистрации нередко используют поддельные или отсутствующие документы. Это позволяет уклоняться от уплаты пошлин и налогов, создает недобросовестную конкуренцию и увеличивает теневой оборот. Отдельная проблема - замена кузова с внесением изменений в регистрационные данные. На практике при такой замене часто предоставляют поддельные документы о происхождении кузова или не предоставляют их вовсе. В итоге фактически легализуются автомобили, которые изначально не проходили таможенную очистку. По данным Кыргызского центра аккредитации, в рамках легализации на технический осмотр обратились владельцы 30 730 автомобилей. Из них 466 единиц (сборные, сваренные или не соответствующие техрегламентам) осмотр не прошли. Успешно прошли 30 264 машины. Государственную регистрацию с уплатой легализационного платежа и присвоением номера региона "10" прошли 30 086 автомобилей. Еще 178 машин, прошедших техосмотр, процедуру не завершили. Общая сумма легализационных платежей составила 1 млрд 811 млн 850 тыс. сомов. "Продление запрета должно сократить возможности для незаконной сборки и легализации автомобилей, повысить собираемость таможенных платежей, уменьшить теневой оборот и допустить к эксплуатации только машины, прошедшие полноценное таможенное и техническое оформление. Мера вводится в рамках права государств - членов ЕАЭС на временные односторонние нетарифные ограничения сроком до шести месяцев", - указано в справке-обосновании. https://www.ng.ru/kartblansh/2026-10-20/.body: Фото Reuters Конституционный суд Грузии приступает к рассмотрению одного из наиболее резонансных политических дел последних лет – конституционного иска о запрете деятельности пяти оппозиционных партий. С соответствующим требованием в суд обратились 88 депутатов парламента Грузии, представляющих правящую партию «Грузинская мечта». Речь идет о партиях «Единое национальное движение», «Коалиция за перемены», «Сильная Грузия – Лело», «Федералисты» и «За Грузию» бывшего премьер-министра Георгия Гахария. Правящая партия утверждает, что деятельность указанных политических объединений противоречит Конституции Грузии, в частности положениям, запрещающим деятельность партий, направленную на свержение или насильственное изменение конституционного строя страны. Конституционный суд принял иск к рассмотрению по существу. Дело будет рассматривать пленум суда, а слушания назначены на 21, 22 и 23 октября. Таким образом, речь пока идет не о запрете оппозиционных партий, а о начале судебного разбирательства, по итогам которого суд должен установить, имеются ли конституционные основания для прекращения их деятельности. Весь процесс может растянуться на девять месяцев и в итоге подвести страну к парламентским выборам 2028 года без уже привычных оппозиционных политических игроков. В случае удовлетворения иска последствия могут затронуть не только сами политические объединения, но и дальнейшую политическую деятельность связанных с ними лиц. Реакция оппозиции, в свою очередь, еще раз указывает на ее глубинный кризис. Часть оппозиционных сил согласилась защищать свои позиции в Конституционном суде. Другая просто заявила о том, что в стране формируется диктатура, и назвала своей главной целью донести это сообщение до всего «цивилизованного мира». В первую очередь до европейских коллег, которых они последние два года призывают активно вмешиваться во внутренние дела Грузии и наносить правительству «Грузинской мечты» политический урон посредством различных экономических, политических и дипломатических санкций. Но, кажется, Европа все-таки опасается вступать в столь глубокую конфронтацию с правительством, понимая, что нынешняя власть, какой бы она ни была, имеет значительную поддержку общества. Запрещать определенные партии или нет – тема не новая. После смены власти, когда в 2012 году «Единое национальное движение» уступило место «Грузинской мечте», и окончательного завершения транзита власти в 2013 году многие политические деятели, аналитики и эксперты призывали «Грузинскую мечту» запретить «Единое национальное движение» и отстранить его главных лидеров от политической деятельности, чтобы, во-первых, восстановить справедливость в связи с теми правонарушениями, в которых эти люди участвовали, а во-вторых, предотвратить распространение их влияния в дальнейшем на политическую, экономическую и другие сферы деятельности. Однако Соединенные Штаты Америки и часть европейского истеблишмента видели в этих силах свои группы влияния, поэтому максимально давили на власть, чтобы сохранить представителей предыдущего правительства в политическом пространстве страны. В итоге эта ставка сработала. И сейчас Европейский союз переживает, что, если Конституционный суд согласится с доводами «Грузинской мечты», политические игроки, на которых европейцы так активно опирались, окажутся официально заблокированы. Следует указать, что главная проблема этого иска даже не в самой попытке запрета определенных партий и политических лиц. В той же Германии, например, звучат призывы признать «Альтернативу для Германии» (АдГ) неконституционной, несмотря на ее феноменальную электоральную поддержку, исходя из поведения партии, заявлений ее представителей и идеологических устремлений. Если опираться исключительно на этот опыт, то бывшая партия власти – ЕНД – должна быть, по сути, запрещена, поскольку это единственная партия, политсовет которой официально поддержал политические процессы, направленные на штурм здания администрации президента Грузии в октябре 2025 года. Многие считают, что ЕНД скорее всего будет запрещена в стране, а ее политические лидеры окажутся в опале. Вопрос, по всей видимости, заключается в другом: насколько сам этот механизм будет действенным и сможет ли он предотвратить, как считает «Грузинская мечта», распространение экстремизма в стране, поскольку все-таки значительная часть оппозиции представлена бывшими чиновниками периода правления Михаила Саакашвили. Смогут ли такие запреты повлиять на формирование действенной и жизнеспособной оппозиции? Нынешняя оппозиция оказалась заложником собственной политической истории, в частности, периода пребывания у власти. Кроме того, она остается заложником непосредственно лидера ЕНД Михаила Саакашвили, который не позволяет оппозиционным силам эмансипироваться от него. В результате они постоянно становятся жертвами его политических заявлений и инсинуаций, а также в целом той политической риторики, которую сами избрали. Эта риторика хотя номинально и является проевропейской, ориентированной на интеграцию в Европейский союз и НАТО, во внутриполитическом измерении носит весьма агрессивный характер, сопровождается радикальными призывами и шагами, которые, судя по всему, не поддерживаются большинством населения. На это указывают и недавно появившиеся в публичном пространстве предполагаемые результаты опроса IRI, согласно которым основные оппозиционные партии в совокупности набирают приблизительно 10%, в то время как «Грузинская мечта» – более 30%. При этом официальное происхождение и достоверность этих данных пока не подтверждены. В ближайшее время Конституционному суду предстоит решить не просто вопрос о запрете тех или иных политических сил, но и определить, насколько такой механизм может быть действенным для борьбы с политическими объединениями, чья деятельность, по мнению «Грузинской мечты», ориентирована не на выборы, а на постоянные протесты, призывы к революциям и смене режима. Конституционный суд, учитывая предыдущий опыт, должен будет очень тщательно подойти к рассмотрению этого вопроса, поскольку не секрет, что в случае принятия решения о запрете партий оно, вероятнее всего, будет обжаловано в Европейском суде по правам человека в Страсбурге. А победа уже на этом уровне для Конституционного суда Грузии и правительства будет чрезвычайно важна. Тем более что до сих пор в ряде наиболее значимых политически чувствительных уголовных дел «Грузинская мечта» добивалась в Страсбурге решений в свою пользу по существу рассматриваемых вопросов. n
